title: Probe-driven fallback and tenant-sensitive circuit policy for regional/tier routing
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a probe-driven, tenant-sensitive automatic fallback controller that triggers safe model-variant fallbacks and circuit-breaker state transitions across region and tier routing. This ticket focuses on the trigger surface, signal fusion, cooldown semantics, and an automated probe lane used to validate fallbacks before wide release.

Background: Current fallback heuristics rely primarily on raw error rates and coarse thresholds. We need a more robust mechanism that: (1) combines multiple signals (429 surge, gateway timeouts, 5xx, p99/p995 latency, queue depth, KV cache miss spikes) into a decaying trip score per tenant+route; (2) validates suspected degradations with synthetic probes and shadow validation traffic; (3) supports soft-open/hard-open circuit states with tenant-level probation and ramped eviction of model variants; (4) prevents oscillation across regions/tiers via jittered cooldown and minimum sustain windows.

Approach:
- Signal model: compute a composite trip score = weighted sum of signal fingerprints (weights configurable per project/tier). Include spike confidence (rate of change) and streak detection (consecutive windows failing). Trip score decays exponentially with configurable half-life.
- Trigger rules: two classes of triggers — advisory (trial fallback via probe lane) and active (immediate soft-fallback). Advisory triggers fire at lower scores and launch probe validation; active triggers fire at higher scores and move to soft-open fallback.
- Probe lane: synthetic, low-QPS directed requests that validate fallback target variants and measure correctness/latency before routing user traffic. Probes run with templated prompts based on route's evaluation set and are audited to avoid data exposure.
- Circuit states: CLOSED -> PROBATION -> SOFT_OPEN -> HARD_OPEN. SOFT_OPEN routes a small fraction (configurable) of traffic to fallback variants; HARD_OPEN redirects all eligible traffic to fallback variant(s) and alerts SRE.
- Anti-oscillation: minimum open window, exponential backoff on reprobing, jitter on cooldowns, per-tenant probation counters, and global mutex to avoid cascading cross-region flaps.
- Observability: new dashboard with trip score heatmap, per-tenant timeline, probe success rate, and fallback volume. Alerting rules for HARD_OPEN events and repeated short-duration opens.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Composite trip score implemented and exposed in telemetry with configurable weights.
2) Probe lane can launch validation traffic for any route and report success metrics.
3) Fallback state machine behaves per spec (soft-open percentage rollout, minimum sustain windows, decay/backoff).
4) No customer requests are routed to a fallback variant until probe validation passes for advisory triggers.
5) E2E tests and chaos tests simulate 429 spikes, upstream timeouts, and latency regressions; system recovers without oscillation in 95% of runs.

Risks: false positives causing unnecessary degradation, probe traffic affecting upstream metrics, tenant isolation complexity, and accidental data exposure via probes. Mitigations: conservative default weights, probe traffic rate limits and scrubbers, and security review for probe templates.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): deploy in staging and a single low-impact region; run probes and telemetry only, no active routing changes.
- Phase 2 (limited): enable advisory triggers and shadow probe validations for 5% of tenants in us-west.
- Phase 3 (gradual): enable soft-open active triggers for non-critical tiers with 1% fallback traffic, expand to higher traffic after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.
- Phase 4: full rollout with HARD_OPEN alerts enabled and SRE runbook.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Patel: Created initial ticket after runbook review from postmortem on 2026-02-28 incident (see Incident-2026-02-28-doc link in Confluence). Goal is to reduce customer-facing degradation during regional overloads without introducing oscillation.

2026-03-11 - Diego Ramos: Proposed composite trip score design. Initial weights: 429s=0.35, gateway timeouts=0.25, 5xx=0.20, p99 latency=0.12, queue depth=0.08. Will make weights configurable per project. Open question: include KV cache miss rate?
2026-03-12 - PM review (Jordan Li): Adds requirement to expose per-tenant audit trail for fallback decisions for compliance-sensitive customers. Added to scope.
2026-03-12 - Design review (Maya Singh): Probe templates must be sanitized; added privacy checklist and template owner. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Probe+Validation+Design
2026-03-13 - Eng sync: Agreed on state machine (CLOSED->PROBATION->SOFT_OPEN->HARD_OPEN). Implement a global mutex for region-level flaps. Diego to spearhead prototype and open PR.

2026-03-14 - Diego Ramos: Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234. Includes trip score aggregator and probe lane skeleton. Unit tests added for decay math and state transitions.

2026-03-14 - QA (Leslie Park): Running chaos tests in staging injecting synthetic 429 bursts against a test tenant. Early results: probe lane correctly launched but probe templates need stabilization (3/10 failures due to prompt variability).
Next steps: stabilize probe templates, implement per-tenant audit logs, add dashboard tiles for trip score and probe success, run extended chaos suite for 72h, then begin canary rollout.

3. Integrate state machine into router/decision layer and support soft-open percentage routing
4. Add per-tenant audit trail and retention policy to compliance store
5. Dashboard and alerts: trip score heatmap, probe success, hard-open alert rule

7. Run staged rollouts and adjust defaults based on telemetry
